title: Righteousness of God
definition: Righteousness of God refers to what Scripture reveals about God's character, work, or relationship to His creation and His people.
summary: Righteousness of God refers to what Scripture reveals about God's character, work, or relationship to His creation and His people.
christFocus: Jesus makes this truth known most clearly by revealing the Father, accomplishing redemption, and bringing believers near to God through the Holy Spirit.

studySections.heading: Doctrine in Summary
studySections.content:
God’s righteousness means He is always right in His character, judgments, promises, commands, and actions. He never bends truth, excuses evil, acts unjustly, or fails to keep what is good.

Scripture presents God’s righteousness as both a standard and a saving hope. His righteousness exposes human unrighteousness, but it also reveals that God acts faithfully to keep His covenant promises and save His people.

The righteousness of God is displayed most clearly in Christ. At the cross, God remains righteous while justifying sinners who trust in Jesus. Salvation does not come by God lowering His standard, but by Christ fulfilling righteousness and bearing judgment for His people.

studySections.heading: Why This Matters
studySections.content:
People often fear that life is ruled by injustice, favoritism, corruption, or chance. God’s righteousness assures believers that the Lord never acts crookedly and never misjudges the truth. His verdict is always faithful.

This doctrine also confronts self-righteousness. No sinner can stand before God by personal merit. The only safe place is Christ, who provides the righteousness sinners lack and teaches His people to hunger for what is right.

studySections.heading: Discipleship and Application
studySections.content: Stop measuring righteousness by comparison, reputation, or religious performance. Confess where your life is not aligned with God’s ways, trust the righteousness given through Christ, and practice what is right even when compromise would be easier.
